title: API Sheriff gateway.yaml
description: JSON Schema for the global gateway.yaml configuration document. Mirrors doc/configuration.adoc field-for-field. Unknown keys are rejected at every object level (additionalProperties: false).

allowedMethods.description: Positive HTTP-verb allowlist. TRACE and CONNECT are never permitted and are excluded from the enum.

version.description: Config schema version; unknown values are refused in code.

cipher_suites.description: Cipher-suite allowlist applied to the terminated HTTPS listener. Omitted leaves the platform default suite selection in force.

passthrough_sni.description: Map of SNI hostname -> topology alias, relayed at L4 without decryption.

management.description: Neutral policy block for the management interface (health and metrics on their own port). TLS POLICY only: the management PORT is deployment-bound and is deliberately not settable here, so the block declares 'port' solely to reject it with an actionable message (ADR-0025).

port.description: Declared only to be refused. The always-failing subschema plus the 'errorMessage' extension puts the actionable sentence at the /management/port pointer, instead of the generic 'additionalProperties' rejection the parent object would otherwise raise.

errorMessage.not: the management port is deployment-bound and is not settable in gateway.yaml: set quarkus.management.port (environment QUARKUS_MANAGEMENT_PORT, default 9000) instead — see ADR-0025

security_defaults.description: Global inbound-filter baseline. An omitted block — or a block without 'profile' — resolves the gateway-wide profile to 'strict'. 'minimal' is a partial disable: it turns off only the url-parameter name/value validation and the per-route pipeline re-run, and is refused at boot on effectively-authenticated and BFF routes (see ADR-0024).

max_authorization_header_value_length.description: Budget for the pre-route 'Authorization' header-value carve-out (ADR-0019). A bearer token plus the 'Bearer ' prefix routinely exceeds the resolved profile's header-value cap (~1028 characters against strict's 1024), which the non-skippable pre-route floor would otherwise reject 400 before route selection. Defaults to 8192 when omitted. Boot-refused when declared below the resolved baseline max_header_value_length, since that would make the carve-out a tightening in disguise.

allow_get_with_content_length_body.description: Admits a Content-Length-framed request body on GET. Defaults to false (omitted = rejected, as before this key existed). PARTIAL relaxation, scoped to two rejection legs on GET only: the body-present leg and the declared Content-Length > 0 leg. Transfer-Encoding on GET stays rejected UNCONDITIONALLY — chunked framing on an otherwise-bodyless method is the shape the request-smuggling defences exist to constrain, and the motivating case (Elasticsearch _search) sends Content-Length-framed bodies, so excluding it costs nothing. HEAD is unaffected on every leg, and the CL+TE and Connection-header framing-strip rules are independent checks that still apply. Gateway-wide because the framing gate runs at stage 1, before route selection.

allowed_methods.description: Global positive HTTP-verb allowlist. An anchor or endpoint may REPLACE this wholesale (no inheritance).

anchors.description: Optional named, namespace-scoped policy anchors. Each anchor OWNS a disjoint path namespace (path_prefix) and carries the policy floor for every route inside it. Every anchor declares two required classification axes: 'type' (proxy/bff/asset; the former 'passthrough' value renamed to 'proxy') and 'access' (public/authenticated). Anchor prefixes must be pairwise disjoint (enforced in code).

upstream_defaults.description: Global retry / HTTP-304 not-modified defaults (both default true). An endpoint upstream_defaults block replaces this wholesale.

asset_defaults.description: Global asset-serving defaults. Add-only: the block extends the gateway's built-in content-type map, it never replaces an entry in it.

content_types.description: Extension-to-Content-Type additions for extensions the gateway does not already map. ADD-ONLY: an entry naming a built-in extension (html, htm, css, js, mjs, json, map, xml, txt, svg, png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, ico, woff, woff2, ttf, pdf, wasm) is REFUSED AT BOOT, not silently ignored. The built-in mappings are immutable because remapping one — svg away from image/svg+xml, or any extension to text/html — is a stored-XSS lever on a security gateway. An extension neither map carries still falls back to application/octet-stream. The VALUE must be a well-formed type/subtype media type, optionally followed by ';name=value' parameters, and carries no control characters: it is served verbatim as the asset's Content-Type response header, so a CR/LF or non-media-type value would be a response-header-injection vector. This schema deliberately enforces only the CHEAP half of that bound — a length cap plus a flat, control-character-free 'type/subtype…' shape. The precise RFC 9110 parameter grammar is enforced at boot by the configuration validator (ConfigValidator.validateAssetContentTypeValues), which additionally names the offending extension and value. Both anchors terminate with a negative lookahead rather than '$', because the schema 'pattern' keyword is evaluated with find semantics and '$' also matches before a final line terminator — exactly the trailing CR/LF these bounds exist to refuse.

edge_hardening.description: Admission budget for the public data-plane edge. websocket_relay_cap is a sub-budget acquired in addition to the general admission permit (a relay holds its permit for the connection's whole lifetime) and must not exceed admission_cap.

allowed_egress_hosts.description: SSRF egress allowlist for 'source: http'. Omitted or empty keeps the secure default, which refuses a JWKS URL resolving to a loopback, link-local, site-local, any-local, multicast, or unique-local address. Each entry names one trusted IdP host that is exempted from that check — widen only for a trusted IdP (threat model GW-05 / BFF-07), never with a wildcard.

tls_profile.description: Name of the logical trust profile used to verify the IdP's server certificate when fetching the JWKS over 'source: http'. This names a trust profile in API Sheriff's own vocabulary; it carries no trust material and no passwords, and the deployment binds the name to concrete trust anchors. Omitted means the JVM default trust store, which is correct for an IdP presenting a publicly-trusted certificate. Name a profile when the IdP presents a certificate from an internal or corporate CA. A named profile that the deployment does not define is refused at startup — it never silently falls back to default trust.

max_sessions.description: Server-mode upper bound on concurrently stored sessions — a DoS guard on the in-memory store. Creating a session beyond the bound is refused fail-closed.

user_info.description: Session/user-info reserved-endpoint settings (fold). The curated identity view the gateway serves to the browser, capped by an operator-owned claim allowlist whose secure default is closed: an empty allowed_claims discloses nothing.

allowed_claims.description: Operator claim allowlist; empty is the secure closed default that discloses nothing. The operator — never the browser client — widens disclosure.

default_view.description: Curated default-view claim selector returned when the caller requests no explicit claims; every entry must lie within allowed_claims.

login.description: Login-initiation reserved-path settings (fold). Mirrors the logout shape so the login-initiation endpoint reads as oidc.login.path.
